topics.title: Review of JSS 2 Work
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to list the basic tools used in garment making, identify different types of patterns, and explain the basic process of garment production.

Introduction:
We have learned about different tools and basic garment construction in JSS 2. Today we will review what we know to build a strong foundation for more advanced work this term.

Content:
The basic tools in garment making include sewing machines, scissors, measuring tapes, pins, needles, thread, and irons. These tools help us cut fabric accurately, sew pieces together, and finish garments properly. Patterns are templates that guide us in cutting fabric pieces for garments. They come in different types like commercial patterns drafted by professionals and basic block patterns which are simple foundation shapes. Garment production involves several steps: taking body measurements, choosing appropriate fabric, cutting fabric according to pattern, sewing pieces together, adding closures like buttons or zippers, and finally pressing the finished garment. For example, when making a simple shirt, we first measure the chest, waist, and arm length, then cut the fabric pieces for the front, back, sleeves, and collar, sew them together, attach buttons, and press with an iron for a neat finish.

Class activity:
Students will work in pairs to identify and demonstrate the proper use of basic garment making tools. Each pair will be given a set of tools and asked to show how to use them correctly.

Evaluation questions:
1. Name three essential tools used in garment making.
2. What is the purpose of a pattern in garment production?
3. List the basic steps in garment production.
4. Why is pressing important in garment making?

Summary:
Today we reviewed the basic tools, patterns, and garment production processes that we learned in JSS 2, which will help us understand more advanced techniques in this term.

topics.title: Advanced Pattern Drafting
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to explain the principles of advanced pattern drafting, draft a basic dress pattern, and draft a simple trouser pattern.

Introduction:
We know how to use basic patterns from last term. Now we will learn how to create our own patterns for more complex garments like dresses and trousers.

Content:
Advanced pattern drafting involves creating custom patterns based on body measurements rather than using ready-made patterns. For drafting a dress pattern, we start with taking accurate body measurements including bust, waist, hip, and length measurements. We then create a basic bodice block by drawing the front and back pieces according to these measurements. For the skirt portion, we measure the waist and hip to create the appropriate width and add flare or fullness as desired. When drafting trousers, we measure the waist, hip, thigh, knee, and ankle to create the basic trouser block. We then add dart shaping for a better fit and create the crotch curve for comfort. Advanced drafting also involves adding seam allowances, notches for matching pieces, and grain lines for proper fabric orientation. For example, when drafting a simple A-line dress, we start with the bodice measurements, create a waist dart for shaping, then flare the skirt from the waist to create the A-line silhouette.

Class activity:
Students will draft a simple A-line dress pattern for a standard size 12 using measurement charts. They will mark all necessary darts, notches, and grain lines on their patterns.

Evaluation questions:
1. What measurements are needed to draft a basic dress pattern?
2. Explain the purpose of darts in pattern drafting.
3. List three elements that should be included in an advanced pattern.
4. Why is the grain line important in pattern drafting?

Summary:
Advanced pattern drafting allows us to create custom garments that fit perfectly by using body measurements to create basic blocks for dresses and trousers.

topics.title: Garment Assembly Techniques
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to demonstrate proper sewing techniques, explain the purpose of lining in garments, and identify different types of interfacing and their uses.

Introduction:
After drafting our patterns and cutting our fabric, the next important step is assembling the garment properly using correct sewing techniques and additional materials.

Content:
Garment assembly involves sewing cut fabric pieces together to create a finished garment. Basic sewing techniques include straight stitching, backstitching for reinforcement, and zigzag stitching for finishing raw edges. When sewing garments, it's important to follow the pattern instructions carefully and maintain consistent seam allowances. Lining is an inner layer of fabric that is sewn to the garment for several purposes: it provides a neat finish inside the garment, adds warmth, makes the garment hang better, and can make it easier to put on and take off. Lining is commonly used in dresses, jackets, and formal wear. Interfacing is a fabric used to add structure and support to specific areas of a garment. There are different types of interfacing: fusible interfacing that is ironed on, sew-in interfacing that is stitched in place, and lightweight interfacing for delicate fabrics. Interfacing is used in collars, cuffs, waistbands, and button plackets to maintain their shape. For example, when making a shirt, we use interfacing in the collar and cuffs to keep them stiff and crisp, while the body of the shirt might be lined for comfort.

Class activity:
Students will practice sewing different seam techniques on scrap fabric, then demonstrate how to apply fusible interfacing to a fabric sample and how to attach a lining to a simple garment.

Evaluation questions:
1. What are the three basic sewing techniques mentioned in the lesson?
2. Explain why lining is used in garments.
3. Name three types of interfacing and their uses.
4. Which parts of a garment typically require interfacing?

Summary:
Proper garment assembly involves mastering sewing techniques, understanding when and how to use lining, and selecting the right interfacing to give structure to different parts of the garment.

topics.title: Finishing High-Quality Garments Ed
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to explain different types of garment finishes, demonstrate proper pressing techniques, and identify quality indicators in finished garments.

Introduction:
A well-made garment is not just about sewing pieces together; the finishing touches determine how professional and long-lasting the garment will be.

Content:
Finishing techniques are the final steps in garment making that give it a professional appearance and durability. Edge finishes include techniques like hemming, which can be done by hand or machine, and serging to prevent fraying. Bias binding is used to finish raw edges on curved areas. Seam finishes include pinking, zigzag stitching, or overlocking to prevent seams from fraying. Pressing is a crucial technique that uses heat and pressure to set stitches, remove wrinkles, and shape garments. Professional pressing involves using the right temperature for the fabric, pressing with an up-and-down motion rather than sliding the iron, and using a press cloth for delicate fabrics. Quality indicators in finished garments include even stitching without skipped stitches, proper seam allowances, neat and secure hems, matching patterns at seams, and well-placed closures. For example, when finishing a dress, we would press each seam as we sew it, then press the entire garment after completion, paying special attention to collar points, sleeve caps, and hem edges for a crisp finish.

Class activity:
Students will practice different edge finishing techniques on fabric samples and then press a partially completed garment, demonstrating proper pressing techniques for different fabric types.

Evaluation questions:
1. Name three edge finishing techniques used in garment making.
2. Explain the correct way to press a garment.
3. What are three quality indicators of a well-finished garment?
4. Why is pressing important in garment making?

Summary:
Proper finishing techniques and professional pressing are essential for creating high-quality garments that look good and last longer.

topics.title: Mid-Term Examination
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to demonstrate knowledge of tools, patterns, garment assembly, and finishing techniques through written and practical examination.

Introduction:
Today we will have our mid-term examination to assess what we have learned so far this term.

Content:
The examination will cover the topics we have studied this term, including review of JSS 2 work, advanced pattern drafting, garment assembly techniques, and finishing high-quality garments. The examination will have two parts: a written section with multiple choice, short answer, and diagram labeling questions, and a practical section where students will demonstrate skills like pattern drafting, sewing techniques, and finishing methods. Students should be prepared to identify tools, explain pattern drafting principles, demonstrate sewing techniques, and discuss finishing methods. The written section will test theoretical knowledge while the practical section will assess hands-on skills. For example, students might be asked to draft a simple pattern, sew a basic seam, or demonstrate proper pressing technique on fabric samples.

Class activity:
Students will complete the mid-term examination which includes both written and practical components.

Evaluation questions:
The examination itself serves as the evaluation tool with questions covering all topics studied so far.

Summary:
The mid-term examination allows us to assess your understanding and application of the garment making skills we have covered this term.

topics.title: Fashion Accessories
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to design simple accessories, explain the materials needed for accessory making, and demonstrate basic techniques for making belts and bags.

Introduction:
After making garments, we can create matching accessories to complete our outfits. Today we will learn how to design and make simple accessories like belts and bags.

Content:
Fashion accessories are items that complement and complete an outfit. They include belts, bags, hats, scarves, and jewelry. When designing accessories, we consider the garment they will be paired with, the occasion, and current fashion trends. For making simple belts, we need materials like leather, fabric, or webbing, buckles, needles, thread, and basic sewing tools. The basic steps include measuring the waist or hip size, cutting the material to appropriate length, attaching the buckle, and finishing the ends. For simple bags, we need fabric, lining, handles or straps, thread, and basic sewing tools. The basic steps include cutting fabric pieces for the bag body and lining, sewing the pieces together, attaching handles or straps, and adding closures if desired. Simple bag styles include drawstring bags, tote bags, and clutch purses. For example, when making a simple fabric belt, we measure the waist, cut a strip of fabric twice the desired width, fold it lengthwise with wrong sides together, sew along the edge, turn right side out, attach the buckle, and topstitch for durability.

Class activity:
Students will design and make a simple fabric belt and a drawstring bag using basic sewing techniques and materials provided in the classroom.

Evaluation questions:
1. Name three materials needed for making a simple fabric belt.
2. List the basic steps in making a simple drawstring bag.
3. What factors should be considered when designing fashion accessories?
4. Explain how to attach a buckle to a fabric belt.

Summary:
Fashion accessories like belts and bags can be easily made with basic materials and techniques to complement our garments and complete our outfits.

topics.title: Mid-Term Break
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to rest and recharge for the continuation of the term's work after the break.

Introduction:
This is a well-deserved break after our hard work in the first half of the term.

Content:
Mid-term break is a time for rest and relaxation. Students should use this time to rest, engage in recreational activities, and prepare mentally for the second half of the term. This break allows students to refresh their minds and return with renewed energy for the remaining topics in fashion design and garment making. It is also an opportunity to observe current fashion trends, visit markets to see different garment styles, and perhaps practice some of the skills learned so far. Students should remember to take care of their sewing tools during the break, ensuring they are properly stored and maintained. For example, students might clean their sewing machines, oil moving parts, and organize their sewing kits so they are ready for use when classes resume.

Class activity:
No formal class activity during the mid-term break. Students are encouraged to rest and engage in personal activities.

Evaluation questions:
No formal evaluation during the mid-term break.

Summary:
Enjoy your break and return refreshed for the continuation of our fashion design and garment making journey.

topics.title: Fabric Decoration
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to explain the process of tie and dye.
The students should be able to list materials needed for appliqué work.
The students should be able to differentiate between embroidery and beadwork techniques.
The students should be able to create a simple fabric decoration using any of the techniques.

Introduction:
We have learned about different types of fabrics and their characteristics. Today we will explore how to decorate plain fabrics to make them more attractive and valuable, just like how our market women add colorful beads to their wrappers to increase their appeal.

Content:
Tie and dye is a fabric decoration technique where fabric is tied or folded in specific patterns before being dipped in dye. This creates beautiful patterns like circles, stripes, and waves. In Nigeria, we commonly use dyes from local plants or chemical dyes. The process involves folding or tying the fabric, applying dye, and then rinsing and drying it.

Appliqué is a technique where pieces of fabric are sewn onto a larger piece of fabric to create designs. It is like cutting out shapes from Ankara fabric and sewing them onto a plain white shirt. Materials needed include fabric pieces, scissors, needles, thread, and a base fabric. The designs can represent animals, plants, or abstract patterns common in Nigerian cultural motifs.

Embroidery involves decorating fabric with needle and thread to create patterns. Different stitches include running stitch, cross stitch, and chain stitch. In Nigerian traditional attire like the Agbada, embroidery is used to create intricate patterns that show status and cultural identity.

Beadwork involves sewing beads onto fabric to create decorative designs. Beads come in various sizes, colors, and materials. In Nigerian fashion, beadwork is commonly used on traditional attire like the Gele (headtie) and iro (wrapper) to add sparkle and cultural significance.

Class activity:
Students will work in groups of four to create a small fabric decoration using tie and dye technique. Each group will fold a white cotton handkerchief in different patterns, secure it with rubber bands, apply fabric dye, and then rinse and dry their creations.

Evaluation questions:
1. What are the main materials needed for tie and dye?
2. List three different embroidery stitches.
3. How is appliqué different from embroidery?
4. Describe one cultural use of beadwork in Nigerian fashion.
5. If you were to decorate a plain white shirt for a wedding, which technique would you choose and why?

Summary:
Fabric decoration techniques like tie and dye, appliqué, embroidery, and beadwork transform plain fabrics into beautiful cultural and fashionable items.

topics.title: Digital Fashion Design
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to list three digital platforms used for fashion sketching.
The students should be able to explain the advantages of digital sketching over traditional methods.
The students should be able to create a simple digital fashion sketch using basic tools.
The students should be able to identify key features in fashion design software.

Introduction:
We have learned traditional sketching techniques using pencils and papers. Today we will explore how technology has transformed fashion design, just as mobile banking has changed how we handle money in Nigeria.

Content:
Digital fashion design involves using computer software and tablets to create fashion sketches and designs. Popular platforms include Adobe Illustrator, CorelDRAW, and specialized fashion design software like CLO 3D and Browzwear. These tools allow designers to create detailed sketches, experiment with colors and fabrics, and even create 3D models of garments.

The advantages of digital sketching include easy modification of designs, ability to save and share work digitally, access to a wide range of digital fabrics and patterns, and the ability to create realistic simulations of how garments will look and move. This is particularly useful for Nigerian designers who want to showcase their work to international clients without physical samples.

Basic digital sketching tools include the pencil tool for drawing, color palettes for selecting colors, pattern libraries for adding prints, and layering features for organizing design elements. Just like how a tailor uses different needles for different fabrics, digital designers use various tools for different design purposes.

Advanced features in fashion design software include draping simulation, which shows how fabric will hang on a body, and pattern making tools that create actual patterns that can be used for cutting fabric. These features help Nigerian designers create more accurate and professional designs that reduce waste during production.

Class activity:
Students will use a free digital design platform like Fashionary or Adobe Illustrator (if available) to create a simple digital sketch of a traditional Nigerian garment like the Agbada or Iro and Buba, experimenting with different colors and patterns.

Evaluation questions:
1. Name two digital platforms used for fashion sketching.
2. What is one advantage of digital sketching over traditional sketching?
3. List two basic tools used in digital fashion design.
4. How can digital design software help Nigerian fashion designers?
5. Describe the process of creating a digital sketch from start to finish.

Summary:
Digital fashion design platforms offer powerful tools for creating, modifying, and sharing fashion designs, revolutionizing how designers work in Nigeria and globally.

topics.title: Creating Digital Collections
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to explain the concept of a fashion collection.
The students should be able to list elements that make up a cohesive fashion collection.
The students should be able to create a digital collection with a specific theme.
The students should be able to present their collection concept to the class.

Introduction:
We have learned individual digital design techniques. Today we will learn how to combine these designs into collections, just like how our local market organizes similar goods in sections for easier shopping and display.

Content:
A fashion collection is a group of clothing and accessory designs that share a common concept, theme, or inspiration. Collections are typically shown during fashion weeks and can range from small capsule collections of 10-15 pieces to large seasonal collections of 50+ pieces. In Nigeria, notable designers like Lisa Folawiyo and Deola Sagoe create collections that reflect Nigerian culture and aesthetics.

Elements that make up a cohesive collection include a consistent color palette, similar silhouettes or garment shapes, complementary fabrics and textures, and a unifying theme or story. For example, a collection inspired by Nigerian festivals might use the colors of the Nigerian flag, fabrics like Aso Oke, and silhouettes that blend traditional and contemporary styles.

Creating a themed digital collection involves selecting a concept, developing a mood board with images and colors, creating individual digital designs that fit the theme, and organizing the designs in a logical sequence. The process is similar to how a film director plans scenes to tell a coherent story.

Presenting a digital collection involves creating a lookbook or digital portfolio that showcases the designs, writing a collection statement that explains the inspiration and concept, and organizing the presentation in a way that tells the story of the collection. Nigerian fashion presentations often incorporate music, dance, and cultural elements to enhance the storytelling.

Class activity:
Students will create a digital collection of 5-7 garments inspired by Nigerian cultural elements like traditional festivals, local foods, or natural landmarks. They will create digital sketches, organize them in a cohesive theme, and prepare a brief presentation explaining their collection concept.

Evaluation questions:
1. What is a fashion collection?
2. List three elements that make up a cohesive collection.
3. How does a mood board help in creating a fashion collection?
4. Describe one Nigerian cultural element that could inspire a fashion collection.
5. Why is it important for a collection to have a unifying theme?

Summary:
Creating digital collections involves organizing themed designs that tell a cohesive story, reflecting cultural inspiration and professional design principles.

topics.title: Revision
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to recall key concepts from the term's topics.
The students should be able to demonstrate practical skills learned during the term.
The students should be able to answer questions about fabric decoration techniques.
The students should be able to explain digital fashion design processes.

Introduction:
Today we will review all the topics we have covered this term, just like how we revise our notes before important examinations in Nigeria to ensure we remember everything properly.

Content:
We have covered several important topics in fashion design and garment making this term. First, we learned about fabric decoration techniques including tie and dye, appliqué, embroidery, and beadwork. Each technique has its own materials, processes, and cultural significance in Nigerian fashion.

We then explored digital fashion design, learning about various digital platforms used for sketching, advantages of digital methods over traditional ones, and basic tools and features in fashion design software. We compared these to traditional methods and discussed how technology has transformed the fashion industry in Nigeria and globally.

Finally, we learned about creating digital collections, understanding the concept of fashion collections, elements that make cohesive collections, and processes for creating and presenting themed collections. We discussed how Nigerian cultural elements can inspire collections and how to present them effectively.

During our revision, we will focus on remembering key terms, processes, and techniques. We will also practice identifying appropriate tools and materials for different design tasks, and understanding when to use different decoration and design techniques. This is similar to how a tailor knows which needle and thread to use for different fabrics.

Class activity:
Students will work in pairs to create a mind map of all the topics covered this term, connecting related concepts and noting key terms, techniques, and processes. They will then present their mind maps to the class, explaining the connections they have made.

Evaluation questions:
1. Explain the tie and dye process in three steps.
2. What are three advantages of digital fashion design?
3. How is appliqué different from embroidery?
4. What elements make a cohesive fashion collection?
5. Describe how you would create a digital collection inspired by Nigerian weddings.

Summary:
Revision helps consolidate our learning of fabric decoration techniques, digital fashion design, and collection creation, preparing us for examinations and practical applications.

topics.title: Examination
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to demonstrate their understanding of the term's content.
The students should be able to apply practical skills learned during the term.
The students should be able to answer theoretical questions about fashion design.
The students should be able to complete examination tasks within the given time.

Introduction:
Today is your examination for Fashion Design and Garment Making. This is an opportunity to show what you have learned this term, just like how the final JAMB examination determines your next step in education.

Content:
The examination will test your knowledge and skills in fabric decoration techniques, digital fashion design, and creating digital collections. You will need to recall information, demonstrate understanding, and apply what you have learned.

The examination will consist of both theoretical and practical components. The theoretical section will include multiple choice questions, short answer questions, and essay questions covering topics like tie and dye processes, digital design tools, and collection creation elements. The practical section will require you to demonstrate skills like identifying tools, describing processes, and creating simple design concepts.

You will be expected to show understanding of Nigerian cultural elements in fashion design, as well as knowledge of international practices. Questions may ask you to compare traditional and digital methods, explain the cultural significance of decoration techniques, or describe how to create themed collections.

Remember to read all questions carefully before answering, manage your time wisely, and show your work clearly. Just like during the NECO examinations, proper time management is key to completing all questions.

Class activity:
The examination will be conducted under examination conditions. Students will work individually to complete both theoretical and practical components. After completion, papers will be collected for marking according to the examination guidelines.

Evaluation questions:
The examination will contain questions such as:
1. Describe the process of creating tie and patterns on fabric.
2. List three digital platforms used for fashion sketching and explain one advantage of each.
3. Differentiate between appliqué and embroidery techniques.
4. Explain what makes a cohesive fashion collection.
5. Create a digital design concept for a collection inspired by Nigerian masquerade festivals.

Summary:
The examination assesses your knowledge and skills in fashion design and garment making, providing feedback on your learning progress and readiness for advanced studies.

topics.title: Closing / Vacation
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to reflect on their learning experiences during the term.
The students should be able to set personal goals for improving fashion design skills.
The students should be able to identify areas for further study and practice.
The students should be able to participate meaningfully in closing activities.

Introduction:
Today marks the end of the term for Fashion Design and Garment Making. We have learned many new skills and concepts, and now it's time to reflect on our journey and prepare for the vacation period ahead.

Content:
As we conclude this term, let's reflect on what we have accomplished. We have explored traditional fabric decoration techniques like tie and dye, appliqué, embroidery, and beadwork, which are important in Nigerian cultural fashion. We have also embraced modern digital design tools and learned how to create cohesive fashion collections.

During the vacation, you have an opportunity to practice your skills further. You might visit local markets to observe different fabric decoration techniques, experiment with digital design tools on computers or tablets, or sketch designs inspired by Nigerian cultural events you attend. Just like how farmers prepare for the next planting season during the dry season, you can prepare for next term's learning.

For those interested in pursuing fashion design as a career, this vacation is a good time to research fashion schools, both in Nigeria and internationally, and to start building a portfolio of your work. Nigerian fashion has a growing global presence, and with proper training and practice, you could be part of this exciting industry.

As we close this term, remember that fashion design is both an art and a skill that requires continuous learning and practice. Whether you pursue it professionally or as a hobby, the knowledge and skills you have gained will serve you well in expressing creativity and cultural appreciation through clothing and accessories.

Class activity:
Students will participate in a closing circle where each person shares one thing they learned this term that they found most interesting and one skill they would like to improve during the vacation. They will also complete a simple feedback form about the term's activities and suggestions for improvement.

Evaluation questions:
1. What was the most interesting thing you learned this term in Fashion Design?
2. How will you practice your fashion design skills during the vacation?
3. What area of fashion design would you like to learn more about?
4. How might the skills you learned be useful in your future career?
5. Describe one Nigerian fashion designer you admire and why.

Summary:
As we conclude this term, reflect on your learning, practice your skills during the vacation, and prepare for future studies in fashion design and garment making.
